Synopsis:
The player sided with Nere, but Nere died in combat. Thrinn announces her plan: to travel to Moonrise.

Cluster Contexts:
- UND_DuergarLoyalSergeant_FollowUp.json: This takes place in the immediate aftermath of a fight: the player had sided with Nere, but Nere was killed in combat. Sergeant Thrinn—reacting with grim surprise—announces a change of plans to travel to Moonrise, signaling a new objective after the loss. Off‑screen, the larger conflict around the Emerald Grove (recent goblin/drow attacks, tiefling refugees, and the druids’ ritual to seal the grove) has left loyalties and morale frayed, and earlier choices (helping repel attackers, dealings with figures like Asharak or Zevlor) will influence how others respond. Thrinn’s military, pragmatic tone suggests the party is shifting from immediate defense to a focused mission despite the grief.
- UND_DuergarCamp_LoyalFollowUp.json: You’re at the aftermath of a violent clash in the Emerald Grove: the player had sided with Nere, but both Nere and Thrinn were killed in the fighting, leaving surviving forces scattered and morale low (Novice Grumm’s line reflects that grim discovery). A duergar now steps forward to speak, revealing his intentions for the captive gnomes and putting the party in the position of deciding the gnomes’ fate. Off‑screen the grove is tense — druids led by Kagha are beginning a ritual to cut the place off and tiefling refugees and other figures (trainers like Asharak, leaders like Zevlor) may be nearby or recently involved. You may also have prior contact with the duergar’s small servant gnome (Skickpit) or other NPCs, which can affect available options or how those gnomes are treated. This exchange determines what happens to the gnomes now that the original allies are dead and the grove’s defenders are weakened.
- UND_TheDrowNere_Mutiny.json: Dialogue after you destroy the cave-in and set Nere free. Thrinn has been put in charge of getting Nere out, but it's the player who accomplishes it. Nere almost just died from inhaling poisonous gas, so he's very angry. In this dialogue, you determine the fate of the gnomes as well as Nere and the mutinous duergar.
- UND_TheDrowNere_FollowUp.json: After fighting and killing a group of duergar servants that mutinied against him, Nere takes his rage and frustration out on one of their bodies by kicking it. Once he's done, he takes the players to a nearby broken bridge and explains that he needs reinforcements. The player can promise they'll inform his boss - Chosen Ketheric - or not.
- UND_TheDrowNere_Mindmeld_LeavingRegion.json: When trying to leave Grymforge before freeing Nere, you get a mindmeld from Nere, warning that he will die if you leave. Nere is not physically present in scene - only his voice is heard.

Dialogue after you destroy the cave-in and set Nere free. Thrinn has been put in charge of getting Nere out, but it's the player who accomplishes it. Nere almost just died from inhaling poisonous gas, so he's very angry. In this dialogue, you determine the fate of the gnomes as well as Nere and the mutinous duergar.

After fighting and killing a group of duergar servants that mutinied against him, Nere takes his rage and frustration out on one of their bodies by kicking it. Once he's done, he takes the players to a nearby broken bridge and explains that he needs reinforcements. The player can promise they'll inform his boss - Chosen Ketheric - or not.
When trying to leave Grymforge before freeing Nere, you get a mindmeld from Nere, warning that he will die if you leave. Nere is not physically present in scene - only his voice is heard.
context: You are in the immediate aftermath of a violent clash in the Emerald Grove: the player had sided with Nere, but Nere has been killed in the fighting. Sergeant Thrinn — grim and pragmatic — reacts to that loss and announces a change of plans to travel to Moonrise, shifting the party’s objective despite the recent shock. Off‑screen, the broader crisis (goblin/drow attacks, tiefling refugees, druids beginning a ritual to seal the grove) and prior choices (helping repel attackers or dealing with figures like Asharak, Zevlor, or Chosen Ketheric) shape how other survivors will respond. There may also be stranded or captured gnomes and mutinous duergar nearby; how those people are treated and whether you seek reinforcements can affect what happens next.
